technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt the Spring Cloud Stream / Spring Integration module pattern: each source/sink is a standalone Spring Boot starter module that can be auto-configured and plugged into the existing runtime.

Reuse conventions and abstractions from the referenced Spring Integration WebSocket and AWS extension repositories (ChannelAdapter, MessageSource, MessageHandler patterns) to ensure consistency with existing modules.
Each new module ships with Java 17+ baseline, Maven multi-module layout, @ConfigurationProperties-based options binding, and a consistent 'spring.cloud.stream.<role>.module' property namespace.
Use official/third-party client libraries: Tyrus/Java WebSocket API for U1; AWS SDK v2 (S3, SES) for U2/U4; DataStax Java Driver for U3; SolrJ for U6.

For the HAWQ sink (U5), implement a PXF-aware writer that uses Hadoop FileSystem + AvroParquetWriter to materialize data, then relies on PXF's external table protocol; support both Avro and Parquet output formats behind a configuration switch.

For U7, design a dedicated 'errorChannel' bean (e.g., 'topic.errors.stream.module') routed through Spring Integration's @ServiceActivator with a global DispatcherExceptionHandler; introduce a small exception hierarchy (GlobalException, DefaultException, ModuleSpecificException) and preserve the original 'Caused by' cause chain when staging error payloads.
Provide a per-module Testcontainers-based integration test profile (Kafka, Cassandra, LocalStack for AWS, Solr, Postgres+PXF where feasible) to keep CI reproducible.

U8 is treated as a pure verification/testing increment over the already-GA partitioning feature; no new runtime code is expected, but regression and lifecycle tests for module add/delete must be authored.
assumptions: A single, experienced Java/Spring developer implements the entire increment; no separate UI/UX, DevOps, or release management work is included.
The target framework (Spring Cloud Data Flow / Spring Cloud Stream) already exists; the work is additive (new modules and one cross-cutting feature), not a green-field build.
Product backlog grooming, formal code review, and CI infrastructure setup are out of scope except for a small 'integration testing' bucket to keep the suite green.
Unit tests are written per module; full end-to-end pipeline tests are reserved for the cross-module integration activity.
For HAWQ/PXF (U5), a Dockerized PXF-on-Hawq image is assumed available for Testcontainers; if not, an embedded fake PXF endpoint is acceptable for CI.
AWS modules (U2, U4) target S3 and SES only; no other AWS services (SQS, SNS, Kinesis, DynamoDB) are in scope.

The WebSocket source (U1) is server-push oriented (server-to-client + client-to-server frame ingestion) and does not include STOMP/clustered broker features beyond the reference implementation baseline.
Documentation effort covers per-module README, configuration property tables, and one example 'stream' definition; full user-guide overhaul is out of scope.
Cassandra sink (U3) assumes schema/keyspace are pre-provisioned by the operator; the module focuses on write semantics, batching, and consistency level configuration.
Solr sink (U6) supports both SolrCloud and standalone modes via SolrJ; it does not include Solr schema management.

activities.activity_description: Review existing module layout and runtime; define naming/property conventions; design the error-channel contract (U7) and its intersection with module-specific exception types; produce a short design note covering U1–U7.

Add new Maven modules to the multi-module build, wire shared BOM dependencies, add the common error-channel infrastructure and exception hierarchy (GlobalException, DefaultException, ModuleSpecificException), and set up Testcontainers test slices.

Implement a Spring Integration WebSocket source (server endpoint + client mode option), expose configuration properties (paths, allowed origins, message converters), and write unit + integration tests for bidirectional browser event ingestion.

Build an AWS source with two adapters: an S3 polling/notification source (S3Event via SQS or polling) and an SES inbound mail source. Wire AWS SDK v2 clients, credential provider chain, and per-adapter options; cover both with tests against LocalStack.

Implement a Cassandra sink using the DataStax Java Driver: configurable keyspace/table, CQL/PreparedStatement binding, batching, consistency level, and async write semantics suited to high-velocity variable data. Test with Testcontainers Cassandra.
Implement an S3 sink: configurable bucket/prefix, partitioning strategies, multipart upload thresholds, and buffered async writes. Cover happy path and failure-rollback tests against LocalStack S3.

Implement a HAWQ sink that writes Avro or Parquet files (format selectable via configuration) to a staging location and exposes them through PXF-compatible external table semantics. Includes schema inference, configurable compression, and PXF protocol handling. Most complex module due to format and PXF specifics.

Implement a Solr sink using SolrJ: configurable collection/core, commit strategy, document conversion from payload, and support for both SolrCloud (CloudSolrClient) and standalone (HttpSolrClient) deployments.

Extend the common channel infrastructure so any source/processor/sink can route exceptions to a user-defined 'error channel' (e.g., 'topic.errors.stream.module'). Implement the exception hierarchy, preserve 'Caused by' chain, stage the error as payload, and provide a 'catch=**Exception' style configuration. Verify with HTTP-source-driven failure scenarios across custom and built-in modules.
Author/add tests that verify the data partition strategy is preserved when modules are dynamically added or removed at runtime, exercising the existing GA behavior end-to-end.

Build and exercise sample streams that chain the new modules (e.g., WebSocket -> processor -> Cassandra, HTTP -> error channel -> AWS sink, HAWQ pipeline), including failure-injection cases that traverse the new error channel.
Per-module README, configuration property tables, an error-channel usage guide with the 'topic.errors.stream.module' and 'catch=**Exception' examples, and a sample stream DSL for each new module.
